## Heart failure example

The heart failure dataset contains information on 299 patients with heart failure.  The variable of interest is `DEATH_EVENT`, which records whether the patient survived (0) or died (1) over a 130-day followup period.

```{r}
heart <- read_csv("../../data/heart_failure.csv")
```

There are many different medically interesting variables, but we will focus on smoking status.

```{r}
heart_summary <- heart %>%
  # Make the labels of the smoking column 
  mutate(smoking = case_when(smoking == 1 ~ "smoker",
                             smoking == 0 ~ "nonsmoker")) %>%
  group_by(smoking) %>%
  summarize(died = sum(DEATH_EVENT),
            total = n(),
            phat = died/total)

heart_summary
```

66 out of 203 nonsmoking patients died, and 30 out of 96 smoking patients died.


## Difference in proportions sampling distribution

Two players compete in a trivia contest.  Player 1 knows 60% of facts, while player 2 knows 70% of facts.  $p_1 = 0.6$, $p_2 = 0.7$.

Each player guesses 10 different pieces of trivia.

```{r}
example_phat1 <- mean(sample(0:1, size = 10,
                             replace = T, prob = c(0.4, 0.6)))

example_phat2 <- mean(sample(0:1, size = 10,
                             replace = T, prob = c(0.3, 0.7)))

example_phat1
example_phat2
example_phat1 - example_phat2
```

Let's repeat this experiment 10000 times to visualize the sampling distribution of $\hat{p}_1 - \hat{p}_2$.

```{r}
trivia <- tibble(
  phat1 <- replicate(10000, mean(sample(0:1, size = 10,
                             replace = T, prob = c(0.4, 0.6)))),
  phat2 <- replicate(10000, mean(sample(0:1, size = 10,
                             replace = T, prob = c(0.3, 0.7)))),
  diff = phat1 - phat2
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(trivia, aes(x = diff)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "dodgerblue", color = "black")
```

Now, let's increase the sample size to 50 questions for each.

```{r}
trivia2 <- tibble(
  phat1 <- replicate(10000, mean(sample(0:1, size = 50,
                             replace = T, prob = c(0.4, 0.6)))),
  phat2 <- replicate(10000, mean(sample(0:1, size = 50,
                             replace = T, prob = c(0.3, 0.7)))),
  diff = phat1 - phat2
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(trivia2, aes(x = diff)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "dodgerblue", color = "black",
                 binwidth = 0.02)
```

EX 11.1

Based on the empirical simulation above, what is the probability that player 1 wins the game?

```{r}
# Probability of player 1 win, based on simulation
mean(trivia2$diff > 0)
```

What is this same probability, but using a normal approximation?

```{r}
# Probability of player 1 win, with normal approximation
se <- sqrt( 0.6*0.4/50 + 0.7*0.3/50 )

pnorm(0, -0.1, se, lower.tail = F)
```


## Two-sample proportion Z test

Let's return to the heart failure data.

```{r}
heart_summary
```

We can check the sample sizes for each group to make sure we have enough data to use the normal approximation.

```{r}
heart_summary %>%
  mutate(sample_size_check = total*phat*(1-phat)) %>%
  relocate(sample_size_check)
```


EX 11.2

Under the null, the probability of dying during the followup period is the same for smokers and nonsmokers.  How can we estimate this common proportion in the heart failure example?

Save this value as variable `phat`.

```{r}
# Extract values from summary table
x1 <- heart_summary$died[1]
x2 <- heart_summary$died[2]

n1 <- heart_summary$total[1]
n2 <- heart_summary$total[2]

phat1 <- heart_summary$phat[1]
phat2 <- heart_summary$phat[2]

phat <- (66 + 30) / (203 + 96)
```


Let's complete the Z test, with an estimated common proportion of "phat".

```{r}
se_null <- sqrt(phat*(1-phat)*(1/n1 + 1/n2))

test_stat <- (phat1 - phat2 - 0) / se_null
```

```{r}
2*pnorm(test_stat, lower.tail = F)
```


Let's look at a simulation approach to the same question.  We need to do a "big box" resampling approach where each group proportion (nonsmoking and smoking) is drawn from a box with the same base probability.

```{r}
heart_simulation <- tibble(
  # Nonsmoking group
  phat1 <- replicate(10000, mean(sample(0:1, size = 203,
                             replace = T, prob = c(0.679, 0.321)))),
  # Smoking group
  phat2 <- replicate(10000, mean(sample(0:1, size = 96,
                             replace = T, prob = c(0.679, 0.321)))),
  diff = phat1 - phat2
)
```

Under the null, the histogram of resampled differences is centered around 0.

```{r}
ggplot(heart_simulation, aes(x = diff)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "dodgerblue", color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.012, color = "white",
             linewidth = 1.5, linetype = "dashed")
```

Let's calculate an empirical p-value based on an observed difference of 0.325 - 0.313 = 0.012.

```{r}
mean(heart_simulation$diff <= -0.012) +
  mean(heart_simulation$diff >= 0.012)
```


## Two-sample proportion Z CI

Let's build a CI for the difference in proportions $p_1 - p_2$.

```{r}
se <- sqrt( phat1*(1-phat1)/n1 + phat2*(1-phat2)/n2 )

cv <- qnorm(0.995)

c(phat1 - phat2 - cv*se, phat1 - phat2 + cv*se)
```
